verdicts.proposal_name: P1: Repair the KP14 truth (regenerate integ_results.npz + G_func.csv, fix H/L regime convention)
verdicts.critique:
Necessary and correct in direction, but INCOMPLETE and it walks the model into a knife edge.

(1) The regime fix is right, and I verified the direction the proposer only asserted. kp14_fd.py:99-101 writes G_up = G1 + [mu_L/(mu_L+mu_H)](lam_H-lam_L)G2 and G_down = G1 - [mu_H/(mu_L+mu_H)](...)G2. For a 2-state chain the solution is V_H = Vbar + w_L*D and V_L = Vbar - w_H*D with w_H the STATIONARY probability of the high state. Matching coefficients gives w_H = mu_H/(mu_H+mu_L) = 0.3191, i.e. the fd file assumes the exit rate from HIGH is mu_L and from LOW is mu_H. config.py:257 LAMBDA_L = 0.36719 is normalized on the same 0.3191 and yields an unconditional arrival multiplier of exactly 0.99990 (I computed it). panel_functions_kp14.py:98 uses the opposite convention and gives 1.71728. So the sim is the error, as claimed. NOTE: the diagnosis-phase agent got this backwards ('kp14_fd.py weights G2 by 0.6809, which is the SIM convention') — it read w_L for w_H. The proposer is right and the diagnosis is wrong.

(2) But the fix as written touches only 2 of 6 places. Flipping line 98 without flipping the CONDITIONAL EXPECTATION blocks makes erets and cond_var internally inconsistent with the simulated chain. All of these hardcode 'exit rate from LOW = mu_L, from HIGH = mu_H' and must be swapped too: panel_functions_kp14.py:190-191 (Et_G), sdf_compute_kp14.py:210-211 (Et_A_G), :217-218 (Et_G_sq), :221-222 (Et_lambdt_A_G), plus the two commented test blocks at :243-244 and :250-251. Six edits, not one.

(3) THE UNMENTIONED STRUCTURAL HAZARD. KP14_RHO = 0.015753 (verified). G is essentially util/rho, so the growth-option value is ~63x the flow and the model is running 1.6 percentage points from the transversality boundary rho=0 (which sits at gamma_z = -0.4294). Regenerating G_func.csv under CURRENT parameters therefore does not just 'raise G by 49x' — it makes every PVGO number hypersensitive to gamma_z, alpha, mu_z and sigma_z at the third decimal. Before regenerating, the calibration (alpha, mu_z, gamma_z) should be re-set so rho is comfortably positive (5-8%/yr). Otherwise the repaired 'truth' is numerically fragile in a different way from the broken one, and Proposals 2 and 5 (which both move gamma_x or gamma_z) are operating next to a singularity.

(4) The proposer's PVGO/P = 0.545 projection is a linear extrapolation of a quantity that is 1/rho-driven and it also assumes the 49x G ratio survives the regime fix; it will not, because lambda falls 42% AND rho is unchanged. Treat 0.545 as an order of magnitude, and check it against KP14's own reported average PVGO share before accepting the recalibration.

(5) Quadrature fix (a) is sound. One caveat: uniform-weight averaging over 20001 inverse-CDF nodes converges slowly for the SQUARED integrands (G_up^2, A_mod^2, A_mod*G_up), which are the ones that set cond_var. Add a Richardson/node-doubling check on those five specifically. Also note integ_kp14.py:45-50's existing error trap tests the integrand at eps_max=10 — it is ~0 whether or not quad succeeded, which is exactly why the failure was silent; the proposer's density-mass assert correctly replaces it.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: It produces NO gap and the proposer says so, which is to his credit. Adversarially, the more important point is that it may make the KP14 table WORSE for the paper's thesis, not better. After the repair the economy is exact 2-factor pricing with beta_x identically 1 for every firm (price = VAP + PVGO is homogeneous of degree one in x at panel_functions_kp14.py:165 and :173, and sdf_compute_kp14.py:167 factors Et_x2[t] out of the entire cross-firm block). So rp_i = gamma_x*sigma_x*dt + alph*gamma_z*sigma_z*dt*share_i is a ONE-dimensional cross-section in share_i, and share_i is affine in bm to within the ~3% dispersion of VAP/book. FM spans that exactly. Expect FF ~ FM ~ DKKM at a ratio of 1.00 with all three near the ceiling — i.e. a clean, honest, and completely null KP14 table. That is the right thing to publish, but the paper needs to be ready to say so.
verdicts.salvage: Adopt in full, with: (i) all six regime edits, not two; (ii) a pre-regeneration recalibration of (alpha, mu_z, gamma_z) so KP14_RHO is 0.05-0.08 rather than 0.0158, and re-derive C, A_0..A_3 accordingly; (iii) convergence checks on the five squared integrands; (iv) add utils_kp14/parameters_kp14.py as the shim and COMMIT the regenerated solfiles with the config hash they were solved under, so this cannot silently rot again; (v) before touching any estimator, report mean_t max_sr_t and the population span ratio SR_RFF/SR_linear from the repaired moments — those two numbers decide whether any of Proposals 2-6 is worth building.

verdicts.proposal_name: P2: K priced technology-domain IST shocks over an observable 2-D technology map
verdicts.critique:
This is the only non-mispricing proposal with a theoretically sound mechanism, and it is also the one that most nearly amounts to rigging. Four structural objections, one of them fatal as specified.

(1) FATAL: making z firm-specific destroys the model's stationary cross-section. In KP14 z is an AGGREGATE GBM precisely so that it cancels in the cross-section — project scale Kj = (alpha*z*A(eps,1))^{1/(1-alpha)} (panel_functions_kp14.py:138) and PVGO = z^alph * x * lambda_f * G (line 173) scale ALL firms together. Replace z by z_i = 0.5*exp(... sigma_z*(W @ p')) and the log-z differences across firms become a random walk: sd(log z_i - log z_j) grows as sigma_z*sqrt(2(1-rho_ij)t), which at sigma_z=0.035 over 920 months is 0.43 and rising. Raised to the project-scale exponent 1/(1-alpha)=4 (at the proposed alpha=0.75) that is sd(log K) = 1.7 and GROWING WITHOUT BOUND; PVGO carries z^alph = z^3 on top. This is exactly the non-stationary size distribution that the GS21 diagnosis flagged as a pathology, imported deliberately into KP14. KP14's z is a permanent level shock by design; you cannot make it firm-specific and keep a stationary cross-section.

(2) The transversality repair introduces a worse problem than it solves. rho_i = rho(g_i) is linear in the firm's effective IST risk price, so PVGO_i ~ 1/rho_i is CONVEX and EXPLOSIVE in g_i. I computed it at the proposed alpha=0.75, gamma_bar=-0.175, sd=0.30 truncated at 2.5sd: 1/rho runs 5.8 (g=+0.575) to 10.8 (g=-0.175) to 71.9 (g=-0.925). A 12x spread in growth-option value driven entirely by a randomly drawn discount-rate parameter sitting near a singularity. That, not the 'p(theta).c_t' factor structure, would dominate the cross-section, and it is precisely the convex-in-a-characteristic object DKKM can fit and FM cannot. A DKKM win obtained this way is a win manufactured by a near-singular denominator, and the proposal's own Sharpe accounting (SR* = 3.118/yr) does not model it at all.

(3) Lowering KP14_ALPHA from 0.85 to 0.75 is a deep technology parameter being moved to accommodate a made-up risk-price distribution. It changes alph 5.667 -> 3.000, C 0.0597 -> 0.1055, the project-scale exponent 6.667 -> 4, the entire size distribution, and every A_i. Justifying a returns-to-scale change by 'my randomly drawn gammas would otherwise blow up firm value' is backwards reasoning.

(4) THE REFEREE'S ONE-LINE REBUTTAL. Under this DGP the true expected return is EXACTLY LINEAR in the 100-dimensional bump basis: rp_i = gamma_x*sigma_x*dt + alph*sigma_z*dt*share_i*(p_i . gamma). There is no nonlinearity anywhere. The DKKM-over-FM gap is entirely a statement about how many regressors each method was handed: FM was given two continuous coordinates (tech1, tech2) and DKKM was given a smooth basis over them. Hand FM 100 technology-cell dummies — i.e. the industry portfolios that every empirical asset pricer already uses — and it spans the truth completely with a purely linear method. 'A 100-factor model beats a 7-factor model' is not the virtue of complexity. The proposal's own numbers concede it: with K=6 the gap is 1.12x. The gap is sqrt(K_reachable ratio), i.e. dimension counting.

(5) Credit where due: the algebra IS correct. I verified a(3alpha-1)/(1-alpha) = 2a^2 - a, that E_t[z_i'^a z_j'^a] = Et_z_alph_i * Et_z_alph_j * exp(a^2 rho_ij sigma_z^2 dt) reduces to the existing Et_z_alph2 at rho_ij=1, and that sum_k p_k = 2*sqrt(pi) = 3.5449 for L2-normalized Gaussian bumps at h = grid spacing (measured 3.54490 at K=100,h=0.10; 3.54446 at K=64,h=0.125). The sdf_compute generalization really is six lines and really is O(N^2).

(6) 'Simple economic models' does not survive a 100-shock exogenous pricing kernel with randomly drawn prices of risk, 28% of them sign-flipped relative to KP14's gamma_z, dispersion 6x the mean, and a total HJ bound of 3.12/yr chosen to land on DKKM's real-data Sharpe. That is calibrating to the answer.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: It would produce A gap, but not the one the paper wants to claim. FM with 100 industry/technology dummies — a completely standard, purely linear benchmark — captures the entire truth, because the truth is linear in the bump basis. So the honest reading of the experiment is 'the benchmark was under-parameterized', and a referee will say so immediately. Moreover a large part of the measured gap would come from the 1/rho_i singularity (a 12x convex spread in PVGO from a drawn parameter) rather than from the technology factor structure, and DKKM's advantage in fitting exp/reciprocal shapes over rank-standardized bounded features is itself doubtful: the KP14 diagnosis measured that the rank-linear basis (64.2% of max SR) is WORSE than the raw-linear basis (70.1%), so the DKKM feature map is actively bad at scale-carrying convex functions. Finally, the proposal itself concedes that at the coded GAMMA_GRID the gap is only 1.13x and that the headline 2.19x requires simultaneously rescaling the bandwidth — so the advertised result is a joint model-plus-estimator change, and the estimator half would raise the same 'you tuned it' objection.
verdicts.salvage: Keep the economic core — heterogeneous, priced IST exposure — but get it from INSIDE KP14 instead of from a 100-shock exogenous kernel. Two much cheaper routes. (a) Keep z aggregate and scalar, and make the RETURNS-TO-SCALE parameter alpha_i firm-specific over the empirically standard range [0.6, 0.90] (capital intensity is observable and measurable). Then beta_z,i = [alpha_i/(1-alpha_i)]*share_i varies 1.5x-9x across firms — a genuine PRODUCT of two observable characteristics that FM cannot form, with the SDF still 2-dimensional, transversality controllable firm by firm, no non-stationarity, and every KP14 calibration target intact. Cost: solve G on a ~10-node alpha grid (rho and C depend on alpha). (b) If a technology space is wanted, make the domain deviations STATIONARY: z_i = z_common * exp(y_i) with y_i a mean-reverting OU field over theta, so z_i inherits KP14's permanent aggregate IST shock plus a stationary domain deviation. Use K = 15-25, not 100, keep alpha at its calibrated value, and choose gamma_k dispersion so that min_i rho_i stays above 0.04 — verify by plotting 1/rho_i, not by asserting rho>0. Then report the FM-with-domain-dummies benchmark alongside FM-with-coordinates; if DKKM does not beat THAT, the result is dimension counting and should not be published as complexity.

verdicts.proposal_name: P3: Historical-cost book value plus vintage/count/investment-intensity/cash-flow-volatility characteristics
verdicts.critique:
Structurally the safest proposal on the list and I want to say clearly why: it touches NOTHING the model's economics depends on. sdf_compute_kp14.py uses `book` in exactly one place, the liveness filter `keep = book[t,:] > 0` at line 269, and historical-cost book is positive iff replacement-cost book is. The SDF, the firm's investment policy Kj = (alpha*z*A)^{1/(1-alpha)}, the G solution, the eleven integrals and the entire conditional second moment are untouched. It cannot corrupt the truth. That is a genuine and rare virtue here.

The einsum is correct: K[t1,t2,n] = Kj[t1,n]*alive, so np.einsum('ijn,i->jn', K, (x/z).ravel()) sums each surviving vintage's capital at the (x/z) that prevailed when it was installed, which is exactly the recorded outflow at panel_functions_kp14.py:157. It does depart from KP14's own footnote-12 definition, but as a measurement convention it is defensible and arguably more realistic than marking to replacement cost.

MY MAIN OBJECTION IS THAT THE ADVERTISED MECHANISM DOES NOT SURVIVE ARITHMETIC. The historical/replacement wedge is log(weighted mean of (x/z)_{t1}) - log((x/z)_t), i.e. minus a vintage-weighted average of the AGGREGATE increments of log(x/z) over each project's age. Decompose it: the deterministic drift of log(x/z) is (mu_x - 0.5 sigma_x^2) - (mu_z - 0.5 sigma_z^2) = -0.00284/yr, so over a 10-year mean project life the systematic age effect is -2.8% in logs. The stochastic part has sd sqrt(sigma_x^2+sigma_z^2)*sqrt(age) = 0.1346*sqrt(10) = 0.426 per project. The stochastic term therefore swamps the deterministic one by 15:1. Consequence: at any date t the cross-sectional wedge is approximately age_i times a COMMON, SLOWLY-VARYING, SIGN-FLIPPING coefficient set by the realized aggregate path over the preceding decades — not a stable function of age. Both FM and DKKM estimate a single coefficient vector over a 360-month rolling window (fama_functions.mve_data; dkkm_functions.ridge_regr), so NEITHER can track a coefficient whose sign turns over. The proposed bm x exp(c1*age) interaction has c1 wandering with a random walk. What the proposal actually adds is mostly common-factor noise in bm, which degrades every method roughly equally.

Second objection: historical-cost book is non-stationary. Since log(x/z) is a driftless-ish random walk, the dispersion of log(book_hist/book_repl) grows with the sample, so sd(log bm) grows with T and the burn-in length becomes a free parameter that sets the cross-sectional dispersion of the paper's central characteristic. This is the same pathology the GS21 diagnosis found (sd(log k) growing as sqrt(T) with zero defaults) and it should not be imported deliberately.

Third: nproj and age are near-redundant with size (the diagnosis measured corr(log nlive, log mve) = 0.9871), and invint built as a rolling sum of a Poisson-lumpy agr will inherit the tercile-degeneracy that already breaks the FF 'cma' sort in BGN (q30 = q70 = 0). Check the split before shipping.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, and the proposer honestly says +2% to +5%. Being harsher: I think the realistic number is zero or negative. The only channel is bm x g(age), whose coefficient is driven by a non-stationary aggregate path and is therefore unlearnable by ANY fixed-coefficient estimator over a 360-month window — DKKM included. Meanwhile the cost is real: bm becomes a noisier proxy for the PVGO share, and since eps is only 5.6% linearly / 15% quadratically recoverable from characteristics, a large slice of the added variance is pure unlearnable noise that dilutes every method. FM also gets age, nproj, invint and cfvol as regressors, so the LINEAR part of every new channel goes to FM for free; DKKM only gets the interactions, and the interaction with the largest advertised payoff is the one whose sign flips.
verdicts.salvage: Split it into two independent changes and stop claiming a DKKM gap for either. (a) Adopt the four new characteristics (age, nproj-as-1/HHI-of-capital, invint, cfvol) unconditionally — they are free, they cannot corrupt the truth, and cfvol in particular is the observable that makes 1/d_i learnable, which is the precondition for the heteroskedastic-D multiplier that Proposals 2 and 4 need. (b) Treat historical-cost book as a SEPARATE arm and only adopt it if a pre-run diagnostic passes: regress the true PVGO share on [1, chars] linear vs. [1, chars, all pairwise products] and require a quadratic R^2 gain of at least 0.10 with a coefficient on bm x age that is stable in sign across the 360-month windows. If the sign is not stable, the channel is aggregate-path noise and should be dropped. Also run the L=5 and L=9 character sets as separate arms so the RFF bandwidth change (sd(Wx) rising from 0.645 to 0.866 at gamma=1) is not confounded with the economic change.

verdicts.proposal_name: P4: Recalibrate theta_eps/sigma_eps/sigma_u and the project count so idiosyncratic variance stops being 1/size
verdicts.critique:
The diagnosis is right, the calibration direction is defensible, and the claimed payoff is essentially nil — which the proposer concedes (1.00 -> 1.02 standalone). Three corrections to the proposer's own risk assessment, one of which is a real hazard he missed.

(1) THE STATED RISK IS WRONG. 'A(eps,u) = A_0 + (eps-1)A_1 + (u-1)A_2 + (eps-1)(u-1)A_3 is a LINEAR approximation' is false. It is EXACT. For CIR processes with linear drift, E_t[eps_s] = 1 + (eps_t-1)e^{-theta_eps(s-t)} and likewise for u, and eps and u are independent, so integral of e^{-CONST*tau} E[eps]E[u] d tau gives precisely that four-term expression with A_i = 1/(CONST + the relevant theta sum). It is a closed form, not a Taylor expansion. And A cannot go negative for CIR states: it is an integral of a product of non-negative conditional means. I checked the proposed parameters numerically: at theta_eps=0.10, A_0..A_3 = 4.354, 3.033, 1.370, 1.205, and A(eps=0,u=0) = 1.155 > 0, A(eps=0,u=1) = 1.320 > 0. So Kj = (alpha*z*A)^{1/(1-alpha)} is safe.

(2) THE REAL HAZARD HE MISSED. sd(eps) rises from 0.0239 to 0.402, and A_1/A_0 rises from 0.396 to 0.697, so sd(log A) = 0.280 and sd(log Kj) = 0.280/(1-0.85) = 1.87. Project scale would span roughly 8x per interquartile and about five orders of magnitude across the support, and revenue per project scales as K^alpha. That may actually be desirable (real sd(log market cap) is about 2.0), but it is an enormous change to the firm-size distribution driven by a parameter the proposal presents as a modest recalibration. It also interacts multiplicatively with the mu_lambda/sigma_lambda quadrupling. Model this explicitly and re-check the burn-in and the sparse-3D memory budget flagged at sdf_compute_kp14.py:98-107.

(3) THE ECONOMICS IS THE STRONGEST PART. theta_eps = 0.35 implies an annual firm-TFP AR(1) of 0.70 and stationary sd(eps) = 0.024. Both are indefensible against the productivity literature (annual persistence 0.90-0.95, within-industry sd(log TFP) 0.3-0.6). Restoring theta_eps ~ 0.10 and sigma_eps ~ 0.18 is a calibration CORRECTION with independent empirical support, not a knob turned to manufacture a result. That alone justifies doing it. It is also the right way to remove the size artifact that currently produces negative Sharpes for all three methods.

(4) BUT THE ASSET-PRICING PAYOFF IS ZERO BY THEORY. Under exact K-factor pricing the D^{-1} tilt is worth 1/(2 sigma_f^2 beta'D^{-1}beta), measured at 0.19% of SR* at N=1000 even with d spanning a 20x range. Idiosyncratic risk diversifies; making it more dispersed does not create a premium, it only reweights the diversification. The proposer states this honestly. So this is a realism fix, and should be sold as one.

(5) The heterogeneous-sigma_eps,i extension is a different animal: it is a genuinely new free parameter (a 7-point grid over a 4x volatility range assigned independently of everything, then reported to the estimators as cfvol). Heterogeneous idiosyncratic volatility is a robust empirical fact so it is defensible, but it is an add-on to KP14, not KP14, and it should be labelled as such. It also multiplies the one-off solve cost by 7 (and by 140 if combined with Proposal 2's rho grid).
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No. Two independent reasons. First, the theory: the premium here remains a covariance (rp = B lambda exactly), so the economy stays in the exact-factor-pricing regime where any well-diversified portfolio with the right beta attains SR* to within O(1/N), and heterogeneous d only buys back the undiversified residual. Second, the estimator: even in the best case the target is 1/d_i = exp(-b'x_i), and the diagnosis measured log d as 88% LINEAR in the 5 raw chars — so FM's linear span already captures most of it, and dkkm_functions.rff line 110 rank-standardizes every feature into [-0.5, 0.5], destroying exactly the scale information needed to represent a heavy-tailed reciprocal. The measured evidence is decisive: in KP14 the rank-linear basis attains 64.2% of max SR and the rank-plus-full-quadratic basis 68.6%, both BELOW the raw-linear basis at 70.1%. The DKKM feature map is WORSE at representing 1/d than plain linear characteristics are. Making d more dispersed hands the advantage to FM, not to DKKM.
verdicts.salvage: Adopt the theta_eps / sigma_eps / sigma_u restoration as a standalone CALIBRATION CORRECTION, justified by the productivity-dispersion evidence and by the fact that it removes the d ~ 1/n_live ~ 1/size artifact that currently makes all three methods' Sharpes negative. Report the resulting firm-size distribution against CRSP as a validation target. Drop the mu_lambda = sigma_lambda = 8 change unless the size distribution demands it (it quadruples the sparse-array footprint and pushes PVGO up on top of Proposal 1's 28x). Keep the heterogeneous-sigma_eps,i extension in reserve and only build it AFTER Proposal 2's or 6's unspanned premium exists, since it is a pure multiplier — and before building it, fix the second rank-standardization in dkkm_functions.rff:110, or DKKM will not be able to use the dispersion you create.

verdicts.proposal_name: P5: Heterogeneous operating leverage via a firm-specific fixed operating cost per project
verdicts.critique:
The best ECONOMICS on the list and, I think, a dead end for the paper's purpose. Let me separate those.

WHAT IS RIGHT. beta_x = 1 for every firm is a genuine structural embarrassment and the proposer nails the mechanism: price = VAP + PVGO with VAP = x*K^alpha*A(eps,u) (panel_functions_kp14.py:165) and PVGO = z^alph*x*lambda_f*G(eps) (line 173) are both homogeneous of degree one in x, and sdf_compute_kp14.py:167 hard-codes the consequence by factoring Et_x2[t] out of the entire cross-firm block. Operating leverage is the canonical, heavily documented fix (Carlson-Fisher-Giammarino 2004, Zhang 2005, Novy-Marx 2011, Donangelo et al.), it keeps the SDF 2-dimensional and exogenous exactly as KP14 specify it, it does not touch z or transversality, and the firm's capital FOC is unchanged because a fixed cost does not affect the marginal condition. Of all six proposals this is the one a production-based asset pricer would actually write down.

WHAT IS WRONG.

(1) THE SPECIFICATION IS NON-STATIONARY AND THE CODE SNIPPET IS DIMENSIONALLY INCONSISTENT WITH ITS OWN DERIVATION. The proposal derives f_i = kappa_i x (per-project revenue) = kappa_i * x_t * K^alpha, then writes `fcost = kappa * A_0**(-1)` — a pure constant, with no x and no K. With a constant f and x a GBM with sigma_x = 0.13 over 76 years (sd of log x = 1.13), the operating-leverage ratio f/(x K^alpha) wanders by more than an order of magnitude over the sample. Cross-sectional dispersion in beta_x would then be dominated by the common time-series level of x, not by cross-firm heterogeneity in kappa, and beta_x -> 1 asymptotically as x drifts up. The model is non-stationary in exactly the dimension the proposal is trying to create. The standard fix in the operating-leverage literature is a fixed cost tied to a slow-moving trend (an aggregate wage growing at e^{mu_x t}) or to the firm's own installed capital, which makes leverage stationary and countercyclical in x_t/trend. Without that, the whole thing is an aggregate-path artifact.

(2) THE DEEP TENSION. In a model whose price function is homogeneous of degree one in the single aggregate shock, you cannot get heterogeneous beta_x without breaking scale invariance, and every naive way of breaking it makes the cross-section non-stationary. The stationary versions all reintroduce a scale (trend, wage, capital), which is fine but must be modelled deliberately, not by dropping a constant into the cash flow.

(3) ENDOGENOUS PROJECT REJECTION IS ASSUMED AWAY. With a fixed cost, an arriving project can have negative NPV and the firm should decline it — a free boundary in eps that kp14_fd.py cannot solve. Capping kappa at 0.60 so this never binds is an assumption chosen for solver convenience, and it FORCES firms to accept every project, which is not optimal policy. Internal consistency of the firm's problem is exactly what this lens cares about, and the proposal handles it by fiat.

(4) MINOR CODE ERRORS. The proposed term1 correction subtracts (1-delta*dt)*fcost/(r+delta)*n_t but omits the expected ARRIVAL contribution to n_{t+1}. And the market-premium rescale gamma_x -> 0.572 feeds back into KP14_CONST (config.py:264) and hence A_0..A_3 and KP14_RHO, triggering the very re-solve the proposal claims to avoid.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap:
Almost certainly not, and the proposal's claimed 1.15-1.30x AT THE CODED BANDWIDTH is the least defensible number in the whole set. Two independent kills.

FIRST, IT IS STILL EXACT FACTOR PRICING. After the change, rp_i = gamma_x*sigma_x*dt*beta_x,i + alph*gamma_z*sigma_z*dt*share_i = B_i . lambda exactly. Heterogeneous beta with exact 2-factor pricing is precisely the case the theory diagnosis simulated (beta = 1 + 2*x1, a 3x spread, N=1000) and it found the linear-characteristic span attaining 0.0999 against a maximum of 0.0999 — a ratio of 1.00. With N=1000 you only need ONE well-diversified portfolio with the right factor exposure; you do not need to reproduce w* pointwise. FM can form that. Making beta heterogeneous adds NO unspanned premium and therefore adds essentially nothing to any basis's ceiling.

SECOND, EVEN THE BILINEARITY IS MOSTLY SPANNED. I computed the decomposition using the proposal's own numbers (kappa mean 0.30 sd 0.15, Rev/P mean 0.103 sd 0.06). Writing kappa*s = kbar*s + sbar*kappa - kbar*sbar + (kappa-kbar)(s-sbar), the total sd of kappa*s is 0.0254 and the unspanned residual interaction has sd 0.0090 — so only 12.6% of the VARIANCE of the bilinear term lies outside FM's linear span of {1, grossmargin, salesprice}. FF also gets part of it whenever kappa correlates with size. So even if the exact-factor-pricing barrier did not exist, DKKM's incremental information would be roughly an eighth of one of two premium channels. Realistic DKKM/FM: 1.01-1.04, not 1.15-1.30.
verdicts.salvage: Do it anyway, but for the RIGHT reason and with the right specification. (i) Adopt it as a credibility fix: 'every firm in our KP14 implementation has beta_x exactly 1' is a sentence no referee should read, and operating leverage is the standard, empirically grounded repair. (ii) Specify the fixed cost as f_it = kappa_i * wbar_t * n_it with wbar_t = wbar_0 * exp(mu_x * t) a deterministic trend (or tie it to the firm's own installed capital), so operating leverage is stationary and countercyclical in x_t/wbar_t rather than drifting with the aggregate path. That version also generates a genuine TIME-VARYING conditional beta, which is the one channel none of the six proposals addresses. (iii) Set kappa dispersion from the gross-profitability cross-section and validate against Novy-Marx's decile spread rather than choosing it. (iv) Do NOT claim a DKKM gap from it. If you want the operating-leverage channel to also pay in Sharpe, it must be combined with something that breaks exact factor pricing — which, on this list, means Proposal 2's high-K factor space or Proposal 6's wedge. (v) Before writing any code, run the population span calculation (max SR in span{1, chars} vs span{RFF} using the true rp and cond_var); it costs nothing and it will settle the 1.02-vs-1.25 question in an afternoon.

verdicts.proposal_name: P6: Persistent mean-reverting demand wedge on price with a nonlinear fundamental anchor
verdicts.critique:
This is the proposal that amounts to rigging, and I will name it as such.

(1) IT ABANDONS THE PAPER'S PREMISE. The title is 'The Virtue of Complexity in SIMPLE ECONOMIC MODELS'. The entire point of using BGN, KP14 and GS21 is that the SDF is the marginal rate of substitution of a stated agent and 'the truth' is that agent's SDF. Multiply price by exp(w_it) and E[m R_i] != 1: the model's pricing kernel no longer prices the model's own assets. sdf_compute's max_sr, port and sdf_ret are then not the projection of m onto returns; they are a purely statistical tangency portfolio that harvests an assumed wedge. The paper would be reporting that a nonlinear estimator recovers an assumed nonlinear alpha. That is circular, and the proposer says so in his own risk list — which does not make it acceptable, it makes it a known defect.

(2) NO FRICTION IS MODELLED, SO THE WEDGE IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT. The calibration targets a squared Sharpe contribution of alpha'D^{-1}alpha = 1.79/month, i.e. an annualized near-arbitrage Sharpe of about 4.7 sitting on the table in an economy with a representative agent whose SDF is m. Nothing prevents that agent from taking it. A demand wedge is only economics if someone is constrained; here the constraint is absent and the wedge is a free stochastic process bolted onto the price. 'Segmented markets' is asserted in the defence paragraph but nowhere implemented — there is no second class of investors, no shadow price, no market-clearing condition.

(3) THE PARAMETERS ARE REVERSE-ENGINEERED FROM THE TARGET. The derivation is explicit: start from DKKM's real-data Sharpe of 3.7, divide by sqrt(1000) to get a per-stock IR of 0.0338, multiply by idio vol to get sd(alpha) = 0.00169/month, pick SD_W = 0.15, back out kappa_w = 0.135. RKRV is invoked afterwards to bless SD_W. That is solving for the free parameter that produces the answer and then finding a citation for it. The independent-evidence test this lens applies is: would you have written down kappa_w = 0.135/yr and SD_W = 0.15 without knowing the target? No.

(4) THE RESULT WOULD BE AN N ARTIFACT. The near-arbitrage squared Sharpe scales as N. At N=1000 SR* = 1.36/month = 4.7/yr; at N=250 it is half. The proposer's mitigation — report the RATIO at N=250/500/1000 — is right but incomplete: the DKKM/FM ratio depends on the learnable fraction of alpha, which does not depend on N, so the ratio will look stable while the entire economic magnitude is a diversification artifact. Stability of the ratio is not evidence that the level is real.

(5) A CONCRETE ERROR. The proposal says 'only term1, term2 and the PVGO part carry the wedge; term3 and the cash-flow piece do not'. term4 (panel_functions_kp14.py:197, rate*dt*C*Et_z_alph*Et_x*Et_A_mod(eps)) is the expected value of the NEWLY ARRIVING project at t+1 — it is a component of P_{t+1}, not a cash flow, and it must carry the factor a_i. Omitting it would put a systematic wedge-correlated bias into erets. Given that the proposal simultaneously demands unbundling term4 in sdf_compute_kp14.py:162-165 — the riskiest surgery on the list, on an expression whose -outer(cf/P, cf/P) double-counting correction only works under the current normalization — the error rate on this change would be high and the errors would be invisible.

(6) A SUBTLER PROBLEM WITH THE MECHANISM. The wedge is orthogonal to everything by construction, so all of the exploitable nonlinearity comes from h(chars) = log(P^fund/book), the MODEL'S OWN valuation function. In other words the 'virtue of complexity' would be the virtue of computing the KP14 valuation formula from characteristics. That is a statement about the functional form of a formula the modeller wrote down, not about markets, and its magnitude is a free choice: enrich h (Proposals 3 and 5) and the gap grows; simplify h and it vanishes. There is no discipline on it.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Yes — which is exactly the problem. It would produce whatever gap you want, because the gap is a monotone function of two chosen quantities: SD_W*kappa_w (the size of the assumed alpha) and the curvature of h (the assumed valuation nonlinearity). The proposal's own predicted range, 1.33x to 2.4x, moves purely with an unobserved 'DKKM recovers 70%/85%/90% vs FM 40%/30%/15%' split that is asserted, not derived. As for whether FF/FM could also capture it: FM captures the linear projection of log bm + h onto the chars, and since bm IS a characteristic and h is a smooth function of 4-7 chars, the linear R^2 could easily exceed 0.85 — in which case the whole thing collapses. The proposer flags exactly this diagnostic and its threshold, which is the honest thing to do and also an admission that the result is a knob. Worse: as currently specified the wedge is a deterministic function of observables plus latent eps, so in the population there is no irreducible noise in alpha at all; the split between DKKM and FM is entirely a function of how nonlinear the modeller made h.
verdicts.salvage: There is a legitimate version, and it is a different paper section, not a KP14 tweak. Model the friction rather than the wedge: add a second class of investors (or a constrained arbitrageur with a slow-moving capital constraint) so that the pricing wedge is an EQUILIBRIUM object with a state-dependent shadow price, and define 'the truth' as the SDF of the marginal investor. Then the tangency portfolio is compensated for bearing constraint risk, the near-arbitrage is not free, and the exercise stops being circular. If that is too much machinery, the defensible minimal version is a NOISY-CHARACTERISTIC story rather than a noisy-price story: keep the KP14 SDF intact and pricing correct, but let the ESTIMATOR observe characteristics with measurement error, reporting lags and non-monotone proxies for the latent states. That preserves 'the truth is the model's SDF', it is what the theory diagnosis identified as the ingredient real data has and these models lack, and it does not require unbundling term4 or defending an assumed alpha. Whatever is chosen, do not calibrate the free parameter to DKKM's published Sharpe.

missed_ideas: HETEROGENEOUS RETURNS TO SCALE (alpha_i) — the cheapest KP14-internal way to get heterogeneous priced exposure. In this model beta_z = alph*share with alph = alpha/(1-alpha) COMMON to all firms, which is precisely why beta_z is affine in bm and FM spans it. Let alpha_i vary over the empirically standard range [0.60, 0.90] (capital intensity is observable and measurable from PP&E/assets). Then alph_i varies 1.5 to 9.0 and beta_z,i = alph_i * share_i is a genuine PRODUCT of two observable characteristics that FM cannot form and FF's size-crossed sorts cannot form. The SDF stays 2-dimensional and exogenous exactly as KP14 write it, every calibration target survives, transversality is checkable firm by firm (rho depends on alpha), and there is no non-stationarity. Cost: G on a ~10-node alpha grid, and C = alpha^{1/(1-alpha)}(1/alpha - 1) and A_0..A_3 become firm-specific. This dominates Proposal 2 on every dimension this lens cares about.

KP14'S OWN DISPLACEMENT CHANNEL IS MISSING FROM THE IMPLEMENTATION. In Kogan-Papanikolaou (and Kogan-Papanikolaou-Stoffman) IST shocks DISPLACE assets in place — new cheaper capital competes away the rents of installed capital, which is why the value/growth spread is a risk-exposure spread and not just a duration spread. In this code VAP = x*K^alpha*A(eps,u) (panel_functions_kp14.py:165) contains NO z at all: assets in place have literally zero IST exposure and the entire z channel runs through PVGO. Restoring displacement (e.g. per-project cash flows declining in the accumulated IST level since installation, or an economic obsolescence rate increasing in z) gives assets in place a NEGATIVE and VINTAGE-DEPENDENT z loading, so beta_z becomes a functional of the firm's whole project-age profile rather than a scalar affine in bm. This is inside KP14's own economics, not an add-on, it is the single most defensible way to make beta_z non-affine in the characteristics, and it pairs naturally with Proposal 3's age characteristic — which would then have a STABLE coefficient rather than the sign-flipping one the historical-cost channel gives it.

THE CONDITIONING CHANNEL IS COMPLETELY UNTOUCHED BY ALL SIX PROPOSALS. KP14's prices of risk gamma_x and gamma_z are constants, so the cross-sectional premium on growth-option share is constant, so the true SDF weight function is time-invariant and a single fixed coefficient vector is the correctly specified model. Real data has countercyclical risk prices, and the DKKM/KMZ theory says conditional timing is one of the two channels through which complexity pays. Make gamma_z (or the arrival regime's price) a function of a slow-moving aggregate state, so the true weight is share_i x g(state_t). IMPORTANT CAVEAT the proposals would need to respect: the KP14 RFF feature map has NO time-varying input at all (dkkm_functions.rff appends rf_stand only for model=='bgn'), so a purely date-level state would be invisible to every estimator. The interaction must appear cross-sectionally — e.g. firm-level exposure to the state, or a state-dependent characteristic.

ENDOGENOUS OPTION EXERCISE / IRREVERSIBILITY — the only genuine source of NONLINEARITY internal to the model, and nobody proposes it. Currently every arriving project is exercised mechanically (panel_functions_kp14.py:107 draws arrivals, line 141 installs capital unconditionally). Give the firm an exercise threshold in eps (or a time-to-build/delay option): the value function acquires a kink, PVGO becomes a genuinely nonlinear and NON-MONOTONE function of the state, and the PVGO share stops being affine in bm. This is textbook real-options economics that KP14 themselves discuss, it is exactly the mechanism GS21's default boundary was supposed to supply and does not (zero defaults in 2.16M firm-months), and it is the only listed candidate that makes the truth nonlinear rather than merely high-dimensional. Cost is real (free-boundary FD solve), but it is the honest version of what Proposals 2 and 6 try to get by assumption.

FINANCIAL LEVERAGE. KP14 firms are all-equity. Equity beta = asset beta x (1 + D/E) is a RATIO of observables — the canonical nonlinear-in-characteristics object, standard economics (Modigliani-Miller, and the entire mechanism of GS21, the sister model in this very paper), and it amplifies the value/growth spread that KP14 is about. Adding even a simple exogenous target-leverage rule with char-dependent D/E gives beta_x,i and beta_z,i a multiplicative (1+D_i/E_i) factor that FM cannot form and FF's size-crossed tercile sorts cannot form. It is also the obvious cross-model import within this paper, and no proposal mentions it.

FIRM ENTRY AND EXIT / A LIFE CYCLE. N is fixed at 1000 with no births or deaths, and roughly 5% of firms per month have zero live projects and are handled by masking (sdf_compute_kp14.py:269) rather than by economics. Real cross-sections have young, small, high-PVGO-share entrants and old firms delisting. A birth-death process (i) populates the small/high-idio-vol tail that DKKM's real-data result depends on most heavily — their Sharpe falls from 3.7 to about 1.6 in mega/large caps — (ii) makes age a genuinely stationary and economically meaningful characteristic, which is what Proposal 3 needs and does not have, and (iii) fixes the zero-capital degeneracy properly instead of masking it. It also stops the 'true' universe and the estimator universe from being implicitly coupled (evaluate_sdfs.py:170-171 subsets by firm_ids while sdf_ret is computed over the book>0 universe).

RE-CALIBRATE AWAY FROM THE TRANSVERSALITY KNIFE EDGE BEFORE DOING ANYTHING ELSE. KP14_RHO = 0.015753 (verified), so PVGO is roughly 63x the flow and the growth-option value is hypersensitive to gamma_z, alpha, mu_z and sigma_z at the third decimal; the boundary rho = 0 sits at gamma_z = -0.4294, only 0.079 from the calibrated value. Every proposal that perturbs gamma_z (P2) or gamma_x/alpha (P2, P5) is operating next to a singularity, and Proposal 1's regenerated G inherits the sensitivity. Re-set (alpha, mu_z, gamma_z) so rho is 0.05-0.08/yr, verify that the resulting AIP-vs-PVGO premium spread and average PVGO share still match KP14's reported targets, and only then regenerate the solution files. None of the six proposals treats this as a prerequisite; it is one.

DISPERSION IN THE DEPRECIATION/PROJECT-DEATH RATE delta_i. delta is a single number (0.1) and it simultaneously sets project life, the diversification of idiosyncratic risk (the 1/n_live artifact), mean capital age, and the duration of the fixed-cost annuity in Proposal 5. Capital durability is observable (PP&E composition, structures vs equipment) and heterogeneous. Making delta_i firm-specific is one line in the simulation, it decouples age dispersion from size, it gives duration heterogeneity that interacts with any term structure of risk prices, and it is a far cheaper route to the cross-firm age variation Proposal 3 needs than historical-cost accounting is.

NOTHING IN THE SET COMMITS TO THE PRE-REGISTRATION DIAGNOSTIC, AND EVERY PREDICTED NUMBER IS THEREFORE A GUESS. Every one of these proposals can be scored BEFORE writing estimator code, using only rp and cond_var from the moments pickle: compute per month max_t SR over span{1, chars} and over span{RFF}, and report the ratio. The proposals' predicted DKKM/FM figures (1.13x, 1.03-1.06x, 1.02x, 1.15-1.30x, 1.33-2.4x) are unvalidated assertions; the span ratio is a two-hour calculation that would falsify at least three of them. Relatedly, max_sr is already computed in every sdf_loop (sdf_compute_kp14.py:292) and saved into the moments pickle, but evaluate_sdfs.py never propagates it, so no table currently shows what fraction of the ceiling any method attains. Any proposal that cannot show a population span ratio above roughly 1.5 should not be built.

THE SCALE-INVARIANCE THEOREM NOBODY STATES. KP14's price is homogeneous of degree one in x and of degree alph in z, and the firm's state enters only through K^alpha*A(eps,u). Any modification that preserves that homogeneity leaves beta_x identically 1 and leaves beta_z proportional to the PVGO share — i.e. leaves the cross-section one-dimensional — no matter how many characteristics are added. This is the correct organizing principle for judging proposals, and it implies a sharp test: does the change break homogeneity, and if so, does it do it in a way that is STATIONARY? Proposal 5 breaks it non-stationarily (constant fixed cost against a drifting GBM); Proposal 2 breaks the z-homogeneity non-stationarily (firm-specific random-walk z raised to the power 1/(1-alpha)); Proposals 1, 3 and 4 do not break it at all, which is precisely why their predicted gaps are ~1.0. Only the alpha_i, displacement, leverage and endogenous-exercise routes break it in a stationary, economically disciplined way.
